subject: Provisional SLA ramp & monthly remedy plan for NimHealth
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@nimhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimhealth.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the caching options. Procurement asked me to follow up with our ask around service levels so we can get a vendor packet ready.

Key items from our side:
- Target baseline uptime: 99.9% (we understand you often publish higher figures; procurement needs a 99.9% floor for the first 6 months).
- Latency objective: p95 <= 300ms for text-gen endpoints (measured at our region).
- Monthly remedy: we would like a clear credit formula tied to monthly invoice: if uptime falls below 99.9% in a billing month, credit = (shortfall percentage) * (monthly invoice) with a cap at 30% of that month’s fees.

We attached our red-lined SLA template (NimHealth_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf) and a sample uptime export for the pilot account (uptime_sample_report_q3.csv). Two asks on next steps:
1) Can Redwood accommodate a staged approach where the first 3 months operate at 99.9% floor and then move to your standard baseline after that?
2) What carveouts do you expect for scheduled maintenance and emergency mitigations?

If you can confirm scope + expected credits math, I’ll route to legal/procurement and we can get to signature.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of Procurement — NimHealth
procurement@nimhealth.com

Attachments: NimHealth_SLA_Draft_v1.pdf (pdf), uptime_sample_report_q3.csv (csv)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing

Hi Emily — thanks for sending this over and for the attachments. We’re excited to work with NimHealth. I’ve reviewed your asks and sketched a pragmatic approach below that balances your ramp needs with our operational guardrails.

Summary proposal (staged baseline + remedy):
- Staged baseline: months 0–3 = 99.90% (as requested). From month 4 onward, standard hosted baseline of 99.95% applies, unless we agree to a Dedicated commitment.
- Latency objective: target p95 <= 300ms for standard text generation routes. We’ll include region-bound measurement (east/us-west) and an initial tolerance during the pilot period (p95 <= 350ms for first 30 days while warm caches).
- Monthly remedy formula (proposed): credit = min( (99.95% - measured_uptime) / 99.95% * monthly_invoice, 25% of monthly_invoice ) for months after month 3. For months 0–3 (pilot ramp) apply: credit = min( (99.90% - measured_uptime) / 99.90% * monthly_invoice, 20% of monthly_invoice ).
  - Rationale: smaller cap during pilot helps absorb onboarding variability; full baseline caps apply thereafter.
- Scheduled maintenance: standard weekly maintenance window of up to 3 hours/month excluded; customers may nominate a preferred maintenance window once on dedicated capacity. Emergency maintenance with prior notice will be excluded if we published a mitigation plan.
- Reporting & triggers: service availability measured from our monitoring (we’ll share daily availability scrapes). Credits trigger only after degraded availability is confirmed and an incident ticket/RCA is opened within 5 business days.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Marissa will confirm the billing-side wording for the credit flow and finalize the cap percentages.
2) Ben to say if we want to offer a Dedicated SLA conversion clause (6-month notice + capacity pricing).
3) We’ll pull a DocuSign-ready version of the SLA and send a landing Doc for signature.

I’ve attached a short example calculation in the body of the PDF we’ll send with legal language. Please let me know if the two-tiered credit cap (20% pilot / 25% standard) is acceptable or whether procurement prefers a single fixed cap.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

--
Quoted: "From: Emily Park <emily.park@nimhealth.com>
Subject: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing"

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing (internal)

Grace/Ben — quick internal note on negotiation posture:
- Pilot (months 0–3): accept 99.9% floor but keep pilot cap at 20% as Grace proposed. Operational variability is expected during onboarding (prefix caching, model warm-up).
- Standard (post-month 3): 99.95% baseline with 25% cap. If customer is pricing-sensitive, we can offer an optional 30% cap in exchange for a 12-month committed spend (we should model economics).
- Mandatory clauses: require documented incident tickets for credit eligibility, 30-day window to dispute availability numbers, and a maximum retroactive credit lookback of 1 billing cycle.
- Attachments to include: the redlined PDF from Emily + a short example calculation table (I’ll prepare).

If Ben agrees, we push the staged wording to legal and then to Emily for sign.

-Marissa
Director, Billing & Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

--
(Internal: do not forward outside Redwood until we have final language)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@nimhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: NimHealth Procurement <procurement@nimhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing

Grace — appreciate the clear proposal. NimHealth is willing to accept the staged ramp (months 0–3 at 99.9%, move to 99.95% thereafter) with the pilot cap at 20% and standard cap at 25% as you laid out. A few logistics items before legal signs:

1) DocuSign: procurement needs the executed SLA via DocuSign. Please send the final PDF and routing info.
2) Vendor questionnaire: legal asked for an updated SOC 2 attestation and a brief description of your maintenance notification process.
3) Incident reporting: confirm that Redwood will open and maintain an incident ticket and produce RCA within 7 business days for qualifying events.

If you can confirm those 3 items and share the DocuSign link, I’ll route to our legal and get countersigned. HubSpot: DEAL-9891 will be updated on signature.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Park
Head of Procurement — NimHealth

--

Subject: Re: Initial SLA ask and monthly remedy framing"
